newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Morgan Stanley raises Hong Kong weighting in model.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Stanley raises Hong Kong weighting in model.

text.p: Morgan Stanley strategist Peter Churchouse said on Monday he raised Hong Kong's weighting in the company's model Asia-Pacific (non-Japan) portfolio to 35 percent from 20 percent.
"This change is based on our view that Hong Kong will be a major outperformer over the next 12 to 18 months," said Churchouse.

Since Hong Kong accounts for 20 percent of the total market capitalisation of those markets included in the Morgan Stanley's Asia-Pacific (non-Japan) portfolio, the new weighting represents a significant overweighting compared with the previous neutral or market weighting, Churchouse said.
"We could put Hong Kong's weighting at as high as 50 percent of the portfolio, if we turn more bearish on other markets in the region," he added.
"In the coming cycle, the Hang Seng Index is forecast to go to 27,000 - 28,000 by mid-1999," said Churchouse.
The Asia-Pacific (non-Japan) model includes Hong Kong, Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Philippines, Taiwan, South Korea, New Zealand, Australia and India, he said.
Churchouse said the cash weighting of the portfolio was reduced to increase the Hong Kong weighting. Other country weightings were not reduced.
"We are also overweighted in India (in the Asia-Pacific model), he said.

Morgan Stanley has also overweighted Hong Kong in its model global portfolio, recommending a weighting of 15 percent compared with Hong Kong's three percent of the total global market capitalisation, he said.
